title: Dehumidifier Freezing Up? Why It Ices Over & How to Fix It
h1: Dehumidifier Freezing Up? Here’s Why — and How to Fix It
dek: Frost on the coil is rarely a dead machine. Usually it’s a cold room, a dirty filter or both — and both are fixable.
description: Dehumidifier freezing up or icing over? Learn why coils frost in cold basements, how to tell normal defrost from a real problem, and step-by-step fixes.
intro: A **dehumidifier freezing up** is one of the most common complaints from basement and garage owners, especially when fall temperatures start to drop. You open the front panel expecting water in the bucket and find a sheet of frost — or solid ice — across the coils instead.

The good news: icing is rarely a sign the unit is broken. A compressor dehumidifier works by chilling a coil below the air’s dew point. If the coil gets colder than 32°F, the moisture freezes onto it instead of dripping off. Two things usually push it there — a room that’s too cool for the machine, or air that can’t move across the coil fast enough.
Below you’ll learn how to tell a normal defrost cycle from a real problem, how to thaw and fix an iced coil safely and what to do if your space is simply too cold for a standard unit.

sections.heading: Why does my dehumidifier keep freezing up?

blocks.text: Almost every case comes back to two causes, often working together:

items.label: The room is too cold
items.text: The DOE rates dehumidifiers at 65°F, and below about 60–65°F the coil starts frosting even in a healthy unit. Auto-defrost can usually keep up into the 40s, but around 41°F and below, ice builds faster than it melts. This is the classic dehumidifier freezing up in a basement problem.

items.label: Airflow is restricted
items.text: A clogged filter, blocked grille or a unit jammed against a wall slows air over the coil. Slower air gets colder, and the coil frosts even in a warm room.

items.label: Less common: a fault
items.text: A failing fan motor, a bad defrost sensor or low refrigerant can all cause icing in a warm room with a clean filter.

sections.heading: Icing up vs. frosting up: normal or a problem?

blocks.text: Many compressor dehumidifiers have an automatic defrost cycle. When the coil gets too cold, the compressor shuts off while the fan keeps running, and room air melts the frost — usually within 20 to 30 minutes.

sections.heading: Dehumidifier freezing up fix: step by step

items: **Unplug the unit.** Running it over a solid sheet of ice strains the compressor.
**Let it thaw completely.** Light frost clears in 30–60 minutes; solid ice can take 2–4 hours. Put a towel underneath for meltwater.
**Don’t chip, scrape or blast it with a hair dryer.** Bent fins permanently cut airflow, and a punctured coil ends the unit’s life.
**Clean the filter.** Rinse a washable filter in lukewarm water and let it dry fully before reinstalling.
**Check clearance.** Leave at least 12 inches around the intake and outlet, and vacuum dust from the grilles.
**Check the room temperature.** Use a thermometer at the unit’s height — basement floors run colder than you’d think.
**Raise the set point or fan speed.** A higher humidity target and high fan move more air over the coil and reduce frosting.
**Restart and watch it.** If thick ice returns within a day in a room above 65°F with a clean filter, suspect a fault.

blocks.title: Don’t leave the room damp too long
blocks.text: According to the EPA, mold can start growing on wet materials within 24–48 hours. A few hours of thawing is fine; days without moisture control isn’t.

sections.heading: Stopping a dehumidifier from freezing up in a basement

items: **Raise it off the floor.** A sturdy stand or shelf puts the intake in warmer air.
**Warm the space slightly.** Even a few degrees from a heat register or space heater can stop chronic icing.
**Choose a low-temperature model.** Commercial crawl space units with hot-gas defrost run well into the 30s — see our [best crawl space dehumidifier](/best/best-crawl-space-dehumidifier/) picks.
**Go desiccant for the coldest spaces.** No coil means no ice.
**Seal leaks.** Cold outside air sneaking in through rim joists and windows makes everything worse.

blocks.text: The same causes and fixes apply to Frigidaire and every other compressor brand. Check your manual for the model’s minimum operating temperature and filter-cleaning instructions, and look at our [best Frigidaire dehumidifier](/best/best-frigidaire-dehumidifier/) guide if you’re weighing a replacement.

sections.heading: When icing means repair or replace

blocks.text: If your coils keep freezing up in a room above 65°F with a clean filter and plenty of clearance, the cause is likely internal: a fan that spins too slowly, a defrost sensor that never triggers or a slow refrigerant leak. Check the warranty first — many brands cover the sealed refrigeration system for several years. Out of warranty, a refrigerant repair often costs more than a new portable unit.

If it won’t power on at all after thawing, that’s a different problem; see [dehumidifier not working](/guides/dehumidifier-not-working/). If it runs without icing but the bucket stays empty, try [dehumidifier not collecting water](/guides/dehumidifier-not-collecting-water/).

A frozen dehumidifier almost always comes down to a cold room, a dirty filter or both. Light frost that clears on its own is normal; thick ice that keeps returning means unplug, thaw, clean and reassess. If the space stays cool most of the year, switch to a desiccant or low-temperature unit rather than fighting ice every season, and keep up with routine [dehumidifier maintenance](/guides/dehumidifier-maintenance/) so airflow never becomes the problem.

faqs.q: Why does my dehumidifier keep freezing up?
faqs.a: Usually because the room is too cold — below about 60–65°F the coil starts frosting — or because a dirty filter or blocked grille restricts airflow. Less often, a fan, sensor or refrigerant problem is to blame.

faqs.q: Is it normal for a dehumidifier to frost up?
faqs.a: A thin layer that clears within 20–30 minutes is a normal defrost cycle. Thick ice that builds up cycle after cycle is not, and means the unit needs attention.

faqs.q: How do I stop my dehumidifier from icing up in the basement?
faqs.a: Clean the filter, raise the unit off the cold floor, give it 12 inches of clearance, warm the space slightly or switch to a desiccant or low-temperature model if the basement stays cold.

faqs.q: Can a frozen coil damage my dehumidifier?
faqs.a: One icing event caught and thawed properly won’t hurt a healthy unit. Running it repeatedly through solid ice strains the compressor and can shorten its life.

faqs.q: How long does it take a frozen dehumidifier to thaw?
faqs.a: Unplugged at room temperature, light frost clears in 30–60 minutes and solid ice in 2–4 hours. Never chip or scrape the ice off.

faqs.q: What temperature is too cold for a dehumidifier?
faqs.a: Standard compressor units lose efficiency below about 65°F and struggle with ice around 41°F. Desiccant units and low-temperature commercial models keep working into the 30s. See [how a dehumidifier works](/guides/how-does-a-dehumidifier-work/) for why.
